\begin{abstract}
This document is the index and precise statement layer for a Zenodo priority
bundle freezing the theory stack of an ongoing computer-assisted campaign on
the plane Jacobian Conjecture: the uniform strip-rigidity theorem (Theorem A
and the uniform residue functional); the sheet-number ladder in the Sigray
frame, every rung book-relative: $td\le 5$ emptiness on the canonical book,
the $td=6$ funnel to the residue-A template, the $td=7$ off-axis book empty
at the tower tier on the filed 17-cell perimeter, the $td=11$ conditional
411-row certificate resting on the named fail-closed classes FC1-R and FC3,
and the $td=12$ type-$(3,5)$ list-relative first-death refusal (14 cells);
the normal-form lemma suite NF-Z/NF-D/NF-M/NF-P with the merged-emission
law; the banked depth-stabilization lemma for the residue-A window system
(first-lemma tier: a depth-free kill direction plus a Tougeron $2e+1$
effective decision constant); and the current, deliberately honest state of
the residue-A record: its depth-21 window is nonempty modulo three primes
while every sampled point dies at depth 23, and the deciding depth-23
computation is still running. Residue-A is the unique coefficient-tier
two-pole template and the current compute target, not the whole live
inventory: per \fp{BOOK-TD12.md}, the filed ladder's live frontier is
exactly $\{$residue-A$\}$ plus the unadjudicated above-bound entries
($td$ 8, 10, 12-(2,3)/(2,5), 14), joined by the four single-pole r9/M2
classes at $td=6$, generic off-axis entries, and every $td$ above the
enumerated range. Every statement below carries its evidence tier, its
scope, and its adversarial review chain. The bundle includes the campaign's own
hostile dependency audit (\fp{REDUCTION.md}), whose verdict is that the
end-to-end reduction from a Keller counterexample to an enumerated book entry
is not yet a theorem; that audit is part of the record being timestamped,
not an external criticism of it.
\end{abstract}

\section{Purpose, provenance, and how to read this bundle}\label{sec:purpose}

This bundle timestamps theory, most of it new since the companion artifact
release for the paper ``A Vertex-Gap Obstruction for Low-Degree Strip Pairs
in the Plane Jacobian Conjecture'' (Zenodo DOI \texttt{10.5281/zenodo.21894922};
the Zenodo records are the canonical public artifacts of the campaign). It
contains four layers:

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The document corpus} (bundle root): the promoted derivation and
review documents (\fp{SHEET6-*}, \fp{BOOK-*}, \fp{TOWER-*}, \fp{NF-*},
\fp{DEPTH-STAB.md}, \fp{TDBOUND.md}, \fp{TRANSPORT.md}, \fp{REDUCTION.md},
\fp{AM-CHECK.md}, \fp{CERT-UPGRADE.md}, \fp{AUDIT.md}, \fp{MATHIEU.md},
\fp{notes.md}, and companions). These are working documents: they record
errata, retractions, and superseded readings in place, on purpose.
\item \textbf{The machine layer} (\fp{cases/}): the exact-arithmetic engines and
gate suites that re-derive every promoted arithmetic claim, plus the frozen
certificate data (\fp{cases/towers/}, the emitted residue-A cores, the
depth-21 fiber Groebner basis and sample points). \fp{VERIFICATION.md} lists
one command per suite with its expected check count; all suites are pure
Python 3 standard library except where noted, and all exit 0.
\item \textbf{The adversarial record} (\fp{xmodel/}): the review documents of the
two independent AI reviewer families, including the reviews that broke
claims. Section \ref{sec:record}.
\item \textbf{This summary}: precise statements with pointers into the other
three layers.
\end{enumerate}

Nothing in this bundle claims a proof of the plane Jacobian Conjecture or of
the sheet-number exclusion. The bundle exists because the campaign produces
intermediate theorems and certificates faster than they can be refereed, and
because the honest, evidence-graded form of the record, including its named
gaps, is itself the artifact worth timestamping.

\section{The uniform strip layer: Theorem A and strip uniformity}\label{sec:thmA}

The strip-pair obstruction theory of the companion paper reduces, at every
cell, to one elementary rigidity statement.

\begin{theorem}[Theorem A; \fp{MATHIEU.md} Section 5.1, PROVED + PROMOTED]\label{thm:A}
Let $A,C$ be polynomials over a field of characteristic zero and let
$w\ge 1$ be an integer. If $AC' - wA'C$ is a nonzero constant, then
$\deg A\le 1$.
\end{theorem}

\emph{Priority and the Zoladek engine.} Theorem A follows in two lines from
Zoladek (Topology 47 (2008), Appendix Lemma A.7, who credits Liouville and
uses the same ODE in the plane Jacobian context); Hermoso-Alcazar (2024) has
the $w=1$ case verbatim. The campaign proof was found independently through
the Duistermaat-van der Kallen valuation mechanism and stands as
corroboration; all uses cite Zoladek/Liouville
(\fp{MATHIEU.md}, priority note; \fp{paper2/PRIORITY.md} in the repository).

\begin{corollary}[strip uniformity; conj:R closed]\label{cor:unif}
With the uniform outer residue theorem (\fp{RESIDUE.md} Section 4b), the
depth-two block variety of a reduced strip pair of type $(k,d_2)$ is
$\{A\ \mathrm{binomial}\}\cap(\{a_2=0\}\cup\{R_{k,d_2}=0\})$ at every cell
$k,d_2\ge 2$ in characteristic zero. The strip obstruction theory is uniform
in $(k,d_2)$; the previously open cells $(3,4)$, $(4,4)$, $(5,4)$ and all
$d_2\ge 5$ close.
\end{corollary}

Review chain: \fp{MATHIEU-REVIEW.md} (independent re-implementation, all six
fronts CONFIRMED, ``Theorem A is a real proof''), plus the external-model
reviews \fp{xmodel/codex-thmA-review-20260812.md} and
\fp{xmodel/grok-thmA-review-20260812.md}. Machine layer:
\fp{cases/residue_check.py} (\texttt{mathieu} mode). Scope: characteristic
zero; depth two; strips as defined in the companion paper.

\section{The sheet ladder in the Sigray frame}\label{sec:ladder}

The remaining sections concern the sheet-number (topological degree $td$)
ladder for a hypothetical plane Keller counterexample $F=(f,g)$,
$td(F)=[\mathbf{C}(x,y):\mathbf{C}(f,g)]$, studied through pole towers and
Newton trees in the frame of Sigray's thesis. The campaign's audit of that
thesis found its printed $td\ge 6$ proof incomplete (errata E1 to E10,
\fp{notes.md}; the bound itself is safe by Orevkov, Domrina, and Zoladek),
which is why the ladder below is re-proved from the campaign's own kill set.
All results in this section are \textbf{book-relative} (Section
\ref{sec:foundations}).

\subsection{$td\le 5$ and the $td=6$ funnel}

The canonical book at $td\le 5$ is CLOSED: zero surviving configurations,
independent of the AF2 pricing layer (\fp{SHEET6-CAMPAIGN.md};
review \fp{SHEET6-A3L1-REVIEW.md}, all fronts confirmed). At $td=6$ the
single-pole sector reduces to four r9/M2 classes, and the two-pole sector
funnels to a unique rigid template: the \textbf{residue-A} object, with
merged child $(6,12,3,2,5)$ at level $0$, gauge $\sigma=6$, pole-position
ratio $a_1/a_2=2\pm\sqrt3$, $\kappa=42$
(\fp{SHEET6-2POLE.md}, \fp{SHEET6-TEMPLATE.md}). Section \ref{sec:residueA}
is the current state of that object. The single-pole analysis is
td-uniform: for every prime $td$, all single-pole configurations die at
entry (Theorem TDU, \fp{SHEET6-TDUNIFORM.md}, PROMOTED), while composite
$td$ retain growing survivor lists ($4$ to $212$ over $td=6$ to $16$), so no
finite residual list exists across all $td$ at current kill-set strength.
The on-axis (all $b_i=1$) books for $td=6$ to $14$ are enumerated in
\fp{BOOK-ENUM.md}: 421 cells, 346 killed inline, 75 survivors, no root cell
surviving anywhere.

\subsection{The $td=7$ panel: census, H5a, and the uniform tower theorem}

Three promoted layers close the off-axis $td=7$ book.

\emph{(a) The zero-chain law.} On the 62-cell class-B/C book the
Proposition 8.1(iv) local solve has a closed-form verdict: a cell is
T1-dead iff $d_p\mid d_q$, iff $\bar\kappa\in\{3,4\}$; 56 of 62 cells die
(\fp{BOOK-OFFAXIS.md} Section 11; dual verification, zero-shared-reasoning
engine check 62/62 plus hostile audit).

\emph{(b) The E5-corrected census and H5a.} The corrected zero-edge pin
$\bar\kappa=(\mu_0\nu_G w_U-2)/(\mu_0-1)$ re-enumerates the book cap-free:
\textbf{17 cells, 238 raw / 233 deduplicated routes}
(\fp{BOOK-OFFAXIS.md} Section 11a; engine \fp{cases/td7_census_e5.py}).
The reading ambiguity H5a in the underlying thesis statement was
\textbf{resolved} on 2026-08-13: the Q-value + E5 reading is proved forced
(\fp{xmodel/sol-h5a.md}; hostile review \fp{xmodel/grok-h5a-review.md},
SOUND), making the 17-cell census unconditional across the coherent
readings; the alternative forced-$\nu$ sub-book (2 cells) is recorded
alongside, and conjecture U\_7C is moot for $td=7$.

\emph{(c) The uniform tower theorem.}

\begin{theorem}[td-7 tower uniformity; \fp{TOWER-UNIFORM.md}, PROMOTED 2026-08-14]
Every cell of the E5-corrected $td=7$ class-B/C book dies at the tower
tier: for each of the 17 census cells, no realization of any filed
completion route (over all recorded arrivals and their $M_U$ classes, all
free characteristics, all neutral padding, all zero-cost insertions, all
terminals, and rerouting of E5-refuted arrival vertices through legal pads)
admits a global Proposition 4.2 approximate-root ladder: level 1 of every
ladder is obstructed by the X / first-charged clash. Class B is empty
before this tier. Hence the $td=7$ off-axis book is EMPTY at the tower
tier.
\end{theorem}

Proof structure: the panel-constant clash plus four lemmas (L-A chain-1
freeze; AM first-charged menu; WIN window emptiness; E5F, the uniform
vertex-level E5 offset law $n=\nu_U\bar\kappa_G-\nu_G\bar\kappa_U\ge 1$)
plus a frozen 16-row witness table. Machine gate: \fp{cases/tower_check.py},
\textbf{1559 checks} plus 21 certificate-suite perturbations, final line
\texttt{UNIFORM (17 cells): THEOREM}. Review chain (seven passes, three
model families): \fp{xmodel/grok-tower-review.md},
\fp{xmodel/sol-tower-review.md} and re-reviews,
\fp{xmodel/grok-t10-review.md}, \fp{xmodel/grok-t58-t25-review.md}, then
\fp{xmodel/grok-uniform-review.md} + \fp{xmodel/sol-uniform-review.md}
(both green; 14 errata folded). Scope, stated in the theorem's own Section
4: an obstruction over the filed route perimeter, not a statement about
convergence, P-realizability, or existence away from the represented
charts. Consequence: off-axis $td=7$ needs no coefficient emitter.

\begin{lemma}[merged-emission law, FC5-D; \fp{TOWER-TD11.md} Section 18]\label{lem:emission}
The post-merge P0 state emitted by a $\nu\ge 2$ merge is schema-determined,
independent of the coefficient type:
\[
w' \;=\; \frac{\bar\kappa\,(d_q-1)}{\nu\, d_q},
\qquad M' \;=\; \gcd(d_p,d_q),
\]
with companion $\rho=\bar\kappa/d_q$. Verified as an algebraic identity on
all three chain families and against the promoted trunk certificate at the
merge itself ($5\cdot 14/105=2/3$; $2/5$; $3/4$).
\end{lemma}

\begin{conjecture}[\fp{TDBOUND.md}]
For every dominant GGV-standard $(m,n)$ pair in rectangular normal form,

\end{conjecture}

\section{The normal-form lemma suite}\label{sec:nf}

The suite answers: can the infinite neutral-word and parametric strata of
the tower books be compressed to finite certificates? The answers, each
with its machine gate, are one honest negative and three positives.

\textbf{NF-Z (closed record; \fp{NF-Z.md}; gate 39 checks).} The neutral-word
future-quotient program is CLOSED as refuted: across four review rounds,
three counterexamples (CE1 register, CE2 prefix-delta, CE3 live-factor cap)
show the free zone carries ordered arithmetic that no finite invariant
compresses; the round-3 SD-conditional exchange theorem is refuted (SD is
necessary, not sufficient). What survives and is proved: the in-zone
ordered core ($Z$, $L^*$, $\theta^*$/WIN, composition), Z1 to Z3, and the
fail-closed policies. All six counterexample configurations are themselves
dead. This negative result is banked deliberately: it is why the census
architecture uses depth caps, not quotients.

\textbf{NF-D (depth caps; \fp{NF-D.md}; gate 22 checks).} On mechanism-A
entries the live-neutral-word depth is finitely capped: at $td=7$, $D=4$
(15 multisets, 75 ordered words, complete menu). The $td=11$ depth is OPEN:
with the corrected H8 law ($P/\mu$, $\mu\mid M$), the windows are infinite
residue classes; round 1's claimed $td=11$ cap was withdrawn as fail-open
and is recorded as such.

\textbf{NF-M (the square system; \fp{NF-M.md}; gate 25 checks).} For every
fixed $\nu\ge 2$ discrete merge schema, the Proposition 8.1(iv) coefficient
equation reduces to a square polynomial system, $\hat Q-1$ homogeneous
equations in $\hat Q-1$ orbit unknowns modulo the scaling torus.
Zero-dimensional components give finitely many future-local types (at most
$(\hat Q-1)!$ per schema, PROVED); positive-dimensional components are
retained fail-closed (NF-M-OB1; none observed). Round 2 executes the 67-row
nested enumeration used in the $td=11$ closure above.

\textbf{NF-P ($\nu=1$ and parametric slice; \fp{NF-P.md}; gate 10 checks).}
The square system is $\nu$-uniform; the $\eta$-pole lemma empties the
$\eta$-absorbed $\varepsilon>0$ modes in one line; pure-(b) families have
$\nu$-independent state data with finite congruence-interval partitions;
the $(2,2t)$ x-tail family is uniformly dead beyond a finite head. On the
audited $td=7$/$td=11$ perimeter there are \textbf{zero live parametric
objects}. The honest residue NF-P-OB1 (closure under state-changing steps)
is the standing beyond-core item, cited, not hidden.

\section{Residue-A: the current compute target, stated honestly}\label{sec:residueA}

Residue-A is the unique $td=6$ two-pole template (Section
\ref{sec:ladder}): the unique coefficient-tier template on the filed
ladder, and the current compute target. It is not the whole live
inventory. In the words of \fp{BOOK-TD12.md} Section 5: ``the filed
ladder's live frontier is exactly \{residue-A\} plus the unadjudicated
above-bound entries (td 8, 10, 12-(2,3)/(2,5), 14)''; to that inventory
add the four single-pole r9/M2 classes at $td=6$, the generic off-axis
entries with no completeness theorem, and every $td$ above the enumerated
range (\fp{REDUCTION.md} HIGH 1 and 2, CRITICAL 7). The current record on
the residue-A object itself
(\fp{SHEET6-DIRECTIONB.md} Sections 6 to 8; all emissions and harnesses in
\fp{cases/}) is a \textbf{mod-$p$ window statement, not algebraized, not
characteristic zero}:

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{CORE2, the compressed depth-21 window.} A 22-pivot
fraction-free band elimination (python-flint engine \fp{cases/fastelim.py},
25000$\times$ the exact-engine wall time) compresses the B-frozen no-log
depth-21 residue-A window to identical 27-variable / 45-equation cores at
the three banked primes ($\approx 6311$ terms). All pivots are unit-class,
so the core is \textbf{equivalence-tier on the $W\neq 0$ chart}, not merely
necessary. Gates G0.1 to G0.7 (frozen-pivot replay, cross-prime support
identity, strip reconstruction, independent twin-engine replay, tau
transport, the a3-chamber reproduction, the 36-fiber sweep) all pass.
Files: \fp{cases/directionb_core2_p*.ms}, legends \fp{*.rows.txt}.
\item \textbf{Depth 21 is NONEMPTY mod $p$.} The radical-fiber core solves
in seconds per prime: Groebner basis of 397 elements (not $[1]$) at all
three primes, identical staircase; the fiber locus is 13-dimensional, is
$\mathbb{F}_p$-point-rich (12 of 12 sampled directions produced verified
points), and globally pins the pole scales ($W_1^4=57673$, $W_2^4=53212$
mod $105337$). This is the campaign's first nonempty coefficient-tier
signal, and it is reported at exactly its tier: a mod-$p$ depth-21
germ-window statement. Frozen artifacts:
\fp{cases/directionb_fiber_gb_p105337.out.txt},
\fp{cases/directionb_fiber_points_p105337.txt}.
\item \textbf{Depth 23 kills every sample.} Evaluating the banked depth-23
Row-22 block at the 12 fiber points: \textbf{0 of 12 survive} (36 of 36
point-draw combinations inconsistent). A sampling statement, not a variety
kill. The deciding objects are emitted: the D23-core
(\fp{cases/directionb_core23_p*.ms}, 87 vars / 77 eqs per prime, with a
byte-identity regression to the CORE2 rows) and the quotient-free
compatibility object (\fp{cases/directionb_row22compat_p*.ms}): a certified
rank-4 Schur step reduces the ten deep tails to \textbf{six compatibility
rows} $c=Lb$, so emptiness of that object is equivalent to the depth-23
kill on the chart. All 12 banked points violate at least one row of $c$
(loop closure 12/12).
\item \textbf{Verdict: PENDING.} At bundling time the depth-23 solver lanes
have timed out at their 12-hour caps and a 48-hour extension lane is
running. Both outcomes are
pre-registered: EMPTY at two or more primes kills residue-A at the
window-screening tier; NONEMPTY routes to the point/dimension iteration of
\fp{DEPTH-STAB.md}. No verdict is claimed here.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{lemma}[Lemma DS, depth decision; \fp{DEPTH-STAB.md}, BANKED
2026-08-17 at the first-lemma tier, both routes, not yet an \fp{AUDIT.md}
promotion; gate \fp{cases/depthstab_check.py}, 14 checks]
Let $A$ be the CORE2 coordinate ring localized at the pole scales, and for
odd $D\ge 21$ let $V_D$ be the residue-A window at depth $D$ with
$J_D\subseteq A$ its elimination ideal. Then:
(1) truncation-compatibility (a machine fact: the D23-core contains the
D21 rows byte-identically) gives an ascending chain
$J_{21}\subseteq J_{23}\subseteq\cdots$ in the Noetherian ring $A$, which
stabilizes; mod $p$, all depths nonempty is equivalent to the existence of
a mod-$p$ formal germ.
(2) (Kill direction, depth-free.) $V_D=\emptyset$ at any single depth kills
the germ; the pre-registered depth-23 decision needs no stabilization
theorem.
(3) (Effective live direction, committed.) By Tougeron's implicit function
theorem in Greenberg's effective form, a depth-$D$ point whose Jacobian
minor has $t$-adic valuation $e\le (D-1)/2$ lifts to a true formal germ;
the decision constant is $D^*_{\mathrm{eff}}=2e+1$. At $D=23$, any found
point with $e\le 11$ already decides the formal germ question.
(4) The banked 12/12 sample deaths refute stabilization at $D^*\le 21$;
every statement carries $D^*\ge 23$.
\end{lemma}

The bundle also freezes the honest instrument audits around this frontier:
\fp{AM-CHECK.md} (the Abhyankar-Moh one-place semigroup test: the
characteristic sequence of the template is fully forced and banked, but no
binding one-place check exists on the pinned data; the binding tier lives
on Jelonek's non-properness curve and is not derivable template-locally)
and \fp{CERT-UPGRADE.md} (effective spreading-out certification of mod-$p$
EMPTY verdicts is dead at realistic prime sizes, needing $10^{9}$-digit
primes for even the smallest toy; the alive sub-lane is Nullstellensatz
certificate extraction, demonstrated exactly on banked 12 to 14 variable
systems and already infeasible at 27).

\section{Foundations: transport, and the honest gap list}\label{sec:foundations}

\textbf{Transport (separately scoped).} \fp{TRANSPORT.md} (2026-08-17;
not yet an \fp{AUDIT.md} promotion entry) proves a pre-Laurent T2-to-T4
simultaneous-normalization theorem for the GGV-\emph{selected} standard
pair: a determinant-one target rotation and source rotation carry the
common-corner pair to a lexicographically minimal Sigray-equivalent pair,
with a coordinate-cusp obstruction, an exact target-degree formula, and
signed-axis transport. \fp{cases/transport_check.py} is a regression
fixture for its worked data, not the proof. Conjecture T, the
corner-to-tree map, remains open: \textbf{this is not a G2 closure}
(\fp{xmodel/grok-transport-review.md}). It does not build Eggers-Wall
trees, does not treat the post-Laurent $[P,Q]=x^j$ objects, and does not
bound $td$.

\textbf{The audit.} \fp{REDUCTION.md} (2026-08-16, hostile dependency
audit; cross-reviewed, \fp{xmodel/grok-reduction-review.md}
SOUND-WITH-ERRATA) is the campaign's own verdict on its foundations, and
its inclusion here is deliberate. One freshness rider: \fp{REDUCTION.md}
is frozen at 2026-08-16; on $td=11$ the later \fp{AUDIT.md} promotions of
2026-08-15/17 control (the conditional 411-row certificate, residual wall
FC1-R + FC3), and item 8 of \fp{REDUCTION.md} Section 4 is superseded by
them. Executive verdict: \emph{the end-to-end
reduction, Keller counterexample $\Rightarrow$ GGV polygon data
$\Rightarrow$ sheet data $\Rightarrow$ enumerated book entry, is not a
theorem, in the repository or in the cited literature.} The ranked gap
list, abbreviated (the document states each precisely, with a dependency
ledger and a list of claims that are false as stated, not merely
unproved):

\begin{itemize}
\item CRITICAL: (G1) the literal starting predicate is wrong, and GGV
minimal-pair selection is existential, not a normalization of every
counterexample; (G2) NO transport theorem carries GGV corner data through
Sigray's normalization: the sheet construction does not consume GGV data
as written (\fp{AUDIT.md} foundations entry, verbatim; the separately
scoped \fp{TRANSPORT.md} result above does not close it); (G3) the
GGV-to-sheet arrow is absent as written and
the reduced object is often ill-typed; (G4) no canonical universal endpoint
or full-configuration landing theorem exists, so promoted ladder results
are \textbf{book-relative}: every configuration in the enumerated books
dies, pending a book-landing theorem (the $td=7$ book carries its own
completeness certificate; $td=11$ its conditional one); (G5) no upper bound
on $td$ exists, so a finite-range run cannot reduce JC2 even with complete
books; also the off-axis sector has no general completeness theorem and
the all-$b=1$ books omit post-jump configurations.
\item HIGH: composite single-pole configurations and on-axis composite
books remain open; the Sigray replacement is not end to end, including
Proposition 4.2's constant-leading-part gap, which sits directly inside
the trust set of the $td=7$ tower theorem of Section \ref{sec:ladder};
source version drift is tracked.
\item MEDIUM: contradictory status prose in superseded documents is unsafe
to cite (the corpus marks it in place); implemented artifacts do not prove
per-entry coverage.
\end{itemize}

This scope discipline was adjudicated by both reviewer families
(\fp{AUDIT.md}, foundations scope entry, 2026-08-17) and is inherited by
every theorem in Sections \ref{sec:ladder} to \ref{sec:residueA}.

\section{The adversarial record and the machine layer}\label{sec:record}

\textbf{Process.} Three frontier model families work every role (ideation,
primary research, hostile review, software, software review): Claude
(Fable, Anthropic) as primary researcher, with GPT-family (``Sol'') and
Grok-family models as co-researchers and adversarial reviewers. Promotion
requires hostile review; verdicts are graded (SOUND, SOUND-WITH-ERRATA,
BROKEN, STILL-SHORT, EARNED) and \emph{negative verdicts are kept}: the
record in \fp{xmodel/} includes the reviews that broke claims (NF-Z rounds
1 to 4; \fp{sol-td11-review.md} BROKEN and the exact-core restatement it
forced; \fp{sol-census-review.md} BROKEN and the 252-row repair;
the withdrawn round-1 NF-D $td=11$ cap). Retractions are recorded in place;
\fp{AUDIT.md} is the promotion ledger; \fp{notes.md} is the dated lab
journal, including operational errors.

\textbf{Machine layer.} Every promoted arithmetic claim has a named check
in a gate suite under \fp{cases/}; \fp{VERIFICATION.md} gives the exact
command list with expected counts (at bundling time: 1559 + 21
perturbations for the uniform tower theorem; 24 census checks stamping the
411 rows; 14, 39, 22, 25, 10, 14, 6, 21 for the td-12 book, NF-Z, NF-D,
NF-M, NF-P, DEPTH-STAB, TD-BOUND, and AM suites; all exit 0). The heavy
Groebner computations (msolve 0.10.1) are \emph{not} re-run by the gates;
their inputs are frozen in the bundle as \texttt{.ms} emissions with
\texttt{.rows.txt} legends, and the gate suites verify the emissions'
internal consistency (byte-identity regressions, round-trip re-parses,
Schur certificates, loop closures) rather than the solver verdicts.
